correctness.rationale: At boundary point z=1 of Omega_A={|z^4+iA|<sqrt(1+A^2)}, the defining function gradient (8,8A) identifies gamma_A(t)=1+t(1+iA) as outward normal and curvature 1/sqrt(1+A^2)>0. Direct polynomial expansion factors phi(gamma)=t(1+A^2)H(t,A^2). When X=A^2<=7 all H coefficients are nonnegative; for X>7 Descartes' rule bounds positive roots by two. Substitution v=At makes H(v/A,A^2) a polynomial in 1/A with all positive-power coefficients positive and constant 8(1-v^2), proving strict monotonicity of the interior-return condition and a unique attained tangency threshold. Independently used SymPy to verify the exact Sylvester resultant = -262144(X-1)(X+1)^9 P(X), all 12 negative lower coefficients of P(7+Y), and P(134)<0<P(135). Thus exactly one X_*>7 discriminant root and A_*=sqrt(X_*); double tangency at equality and exactly two simple transverse crossings above follow from sign/Descartes. For large A the implicit-function expansions at v=1 and w=8^(1/5) with t=A^(-4/5)w give t_-=A^-1+31/16 A^-2+O(A^-3) and t_+=8^(1/5)A^(-4/5)-8^(-1/5)A^(-6/5)+O(A^(-8/5)). Finite algebra and sample-root evaluations corroborate; the monotonicity/root bound/IFT establish the continuous theorem.
